title: Fair When Trained, Unfair When Deployed: Observable Fairness Measures are Unstable in Performative Prediction Settings
benchmark_measurement: The paper does not conduct a benchmark related to faith or religion. It is a theoretical paper discussing algorithmic fairness in performative prediction settings, using sensitive attributes like race and gender as examples.
findings: This paper does not contain any findings related to religion, as its focus is on the theoretical instability of observable fairness measures in performative prediction settings.
